+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8480'
+title: 'Ask 4a: let a tool attach a structured, non-model-facing record to its call through ToolContext.attach'
+---
+## What
+Router half of Ask 4, step one. Give a tool a way to hand the Router a structured record of what its call did (for example a file-change set), separate from the model-facing rendered output. The Multitool half (make `FileChange`/`FileChangeSet` public and drain the `FileChangeJournal` at the end of each call) will call this API.
+
+The Router does not know the record's type. It carries an opaque JSON document with a schema name, the same shape `SegmentPayload.structure` uses.
+
+Files:
+- New `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ToolCallAttachment.swift`: `public struct ToolCallAttachment: Sendable, Equatable, Codable { public let schemaName: String; public let contentJSON: String; public init(schemaName:contentJSON:) }`. Doc: `contentJSON` is a JSON document the tool owns; `schemaName` names its type so a host can decode it. Never rendered to the model.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ToolContext.swift`: add a stored `private let attachmentSink: @Sendable (ToolCallAttachment) -> Void` (default `{ _ in }`) to both initializers, and `public func attach(_ attachment: ToolCallAttachment)`. Doc: attachments collect on the run named by `completionToken` and are delivered when the call closes (task 4b). A call outside any run drops the attachment.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ToolRun.swift`: add an internal `final class ToolCallAttachmentBox: Sendable` over `Mutex<[ToolCallAttachment]>` with `append` and `drain`. `ToolRun.init` makes one and hands its `append` to the context. Add `let attachments: [ToolCallAttachment]` to `RunSettlement`, filled from `drain()` in `settle(arguments:)` after the wrapped call returns.
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsRouter/Hosting/ContextBindingTool.swift`: make a box in `bind(arguments:reportingTo:)`, hand `append` to the context, and drain it after the call. Hold the drained array in a local for task 4b to post.
+- Do not change `OperationEvent`; it lives in FoundationModelsExtras.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `ToolContext.current?.attach(ToolCallAttachment(schemaName:contentJSON:))` compiles from a package that imports only `FoundationModelsRouter`.
+- [ ] Inside a `RunToCompletionRunner` call, two `attach` calls give a `RunSettlement.attachments` of two elements in call order.
+- [ ] Inside a `BackgroundToolRunner` call, attachments made after the envelope returns still reach that run's `RunSettlement`.
+- [ ] Inside a `ContextBindingTool` call, attachments drain to the local array in call order.
+- [ ] `attach` on a `ToolContext` built with the default sink drops the attachment and does not trap.
+- [ ] Attachments never appear in the rendered output, in `OperationEvent.detail`, or in any transcript segment.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/ToolContextTests.swift`: `attach` routes to the sink the context was built with; the default sink drops.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/RunToCompletionRunnerTests.swift` and `BackgroundToolRunnerTests.swift`: a stub tool that attaches twice; assert `RunSettlement.attachments` (through the internal `ToolRun`, with `@testable import`).
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/ToolMountingTests.swift`: a non-`String` tool under `ContextBindingTool` attaches and the drained array holds it.
+- [ ] Run `swift build 2>&1` and `swift test`. Expect zero warnings and all green.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd`: write the failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #upstream-asks #hosting #api
\ No newline at end of file
